RECIPE GROUND TRUTH - Caramelized Custard Tart Cups
Category: sweet | Cuisine: Portuguese
Description: These Portuguese-inspired custard tart cups capture the blistered, caramelized tops and shattering layers of traditional pastéis de nata, reimagined for a standard muffin pan. A quick laminated puff pastry base hugs a silky lemon–cinnamon custard that bakes into golden, freckled rounds that lift cleanly from the tin.
Ingredients: 1 sheet (8–9 oz) Frozen puff pastry sheet, thawed; 1 cup Granulated sugar; 1/3 cup Water; 1 stick (about 3 inches) Cinnamon stick; 1 strip (about 3 inches) Lemon peel strip (Yellow part only, avoid white pith if possible); 1 cup Whole milk; 3 tbsp All-purpose flour; 1/8 tsp Kosher salt; 4 Large egg yolks; 1 tsp Pure vanilla extract; 1/8 tsp Ground cinnamon (Optional, for dusting after baking); 1 tbsp Nonstick cooking spray or unsalted butter (Softened, for greasing muffin pan)
Method: 1. Preheat the oven to 500°F with a rack in the upper third. Lightly grease a standard 12-cup muffin pan with nonstick cooking spray or softened unsalted butter, making sure to coat the bottoms and sides of each well. 2. Make the sugar syrup: In a small saucepan, combine the granulated sugar, water, cinnamon stick, and lemon peel strip. Set over medium heat and cook, swirling occasionally, until the sugar dissolves and the mixture comes to a gentle boil. Continue boiling without stirring for 2–3 minutes, just until slightly thickened but still clear. Remove from the heat and let the syrup cool while you prepare the custard base. Leave the cinnamon stick and lemon peel in the syrup to infuse. 3. Make the milk-flour base: In a separate medium saucepan off the heat, whisk together the all-purpose flour and kosher salt. Gradually whisk in the whole milk, a little at a time, until completely smooth with no lumps. 4. Cook the milk mixture: Place the saucepan with the milk mixture over medium heat. Cook, whisking constantly, until it thickens to a smooth, pudding-like consistency that lightly coats the back of a spoon, 3–5 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool for 5 minutes, whisking occasionally to keep it smooth. 5. Prepare the egg mixture: In a medium bowl, whisk the large egg yolks until smooth. Slowly drizzle the slightly cooled milk mixture into the yolks, whisking constantly, to temper them and prevent scrambling. 6. Finish the custard: Strain the cooled sugar syrup through a fine-mesh sieve directly into the egg-milk mixture, discarding the cinnamon stick and lemon peel. Whisk until fully combined, then whisk in the pure vanilla extract. The custard will be fairly thin and pourable. Set aside while you shape the pastry cups. 7. Shape the puff pastry: Unfold the thawed puff pastry sheet on a lightly floured surface, smoothing out any creases. Starting from one short end, roll the pastry up tightly into a log, creating a spiral. Using a sharp knife, cut the log crosswise into 12 equal rounds. 8. Form the tart cups: Working with one round at a time, place a pastry round cut-side up in a muffin cup. With your thumbs, press and stretch the dough outward and up the sides of the well, keeping the spiral pattern on the bottom and forming an even shell that reaches just to the rim. Repeat with the remaining pastry rounds to line all 12 muffin cups. 9. Fill with custard: Give the custard a quick whisk, then pour it into each pastry-lined muffin cup, filling each about 3/4 full. Divide the custard evenly among all 12 cups; you should use all of it. 10. Bake the tart cups: Place the muffin pan on the upper oven rack. Bake at 500°F for 15–20 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through, until the pastry is deeply golden, the custard is puffed with dark caramelized spots on top, and the centers still wobble slightly when the pan is gently shaken. 11. Optional broil for extra blistering: If the tops are not as freckled as you like but the pastry edges look done, switch the oven to broil and broil the tart cups for 1–2 minutes, watching closely, until the custard tops develop additional dark spots. Do not walk away; they can go from perfect to burnt quickly. 12. Cool and finish: Transfer the muffin pan to a wire rack and let the tart cups cool in the pan for 10–15 minutes; the custard will set as they cool. Run a thin knife around the edges if needed, then gently lift each tart cup out of the pan. Dust lightly with the optional ground cinnamon just before serving, if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.

Category: breakfast

Method: 1. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Place an oven thermometer inside if you have one and let the oven fully preheat. Cook, breaking it into small crumbles with a spatula, until browned and cooked through, 5–7 minutes. If there’s more than 1 tsp of rendered fat, drain off the excess. Remove sausage to a plate to cool slightly. 3. Sauté the vegetables: In the same skillet (no need to wash), add the diced onion and both bell peppers. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until softened and just starting to get some golden edges, 4–5 minutes. Add the chopped spinach and cook until wilted and most moisture has evaporated, 1–2 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool for 3–5 minutes so they don’t scramble the eggs on contact. 4. Make the egg base: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the 8 whole eggs and 1 cup liquid egg whites until well combined and slightly frothy. Add the milk, kosher salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, and crushed red pepper (if using). Whisk again until the seasonings are evenly distributed. Don’t shortcut this; uneven seasoning shows up in tiny portions. 5. Add cheese and herbs: Stir in the shredded sharp cheddar, grated Parmesan, and chopped parsley. Mix until the cheese is evenly coated in the egg mixture so it doesn’t clump in one or two cups. 6. Assemble in the muffin tin: Divide the cooked sausage evenly among the 12 muffin cups (about 1 heaping tablespoon per cup). Do the same with the sautéed vegetable mixture, gently spreading it so each cup has a roughly equal amount. Give the egg mixture a quick whisk, then pour it over the sausage and vegetables, filling each cup to about 3/4 full. If you have a little extra, top off the skimpiest cups—don’t overfill past the rim or they’ll mushroom and stick. 7. Bake: Place the muffin tin on the middle oven rack. Cool and release: Remove the pan from the oven and let the egg cups cool in the tin for 5–7 minutes. Run a thin offset spatula or butter knife around the edges of each cup to loosen, then gently lift them out. If any resist, let them sit another couple minutes; the steam will help them release. 9. Store for the week: Let the egg cups cool to room temperature before storing. Ingredients: Cooking spray (or 1 tbsp neutral oil for greasing pan); 8 large eggs; 1 cup liquid egg whites (or about 6 large egg whites); 1/3 cup whole milk (or 2% milk); 1/2 tsp kosher salt; 1/4 tsp black pepper; 1/4 tsp garlic powder; 1/4 tsp onion powder; 1/4 tsp smoked paprika; 1/8 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (optional, for mild heat); 6 oz turkey breakfast sausage (casings removed if linked; I like Jennie-O or similar); 1/2 cup finely diced yellow onion; 1/2 cup finely diced red bell pepper; 1/2 cup finely diced green bell pepper; 1 cup packed fresh baby spinach (finely chopped); 3/4 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese (about 3 oz); 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese; 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley (optional, for brightness); 1 tbsp olive oil (only if sausage is very lean and sticks)
Method: 1. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Place an oven thermometer inside if you have one and let the oven fully preheat. Lightly grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with cooking spray, making sure to coat the sides and rims of each cup to prevent sticking. 2. Cook the sausage: In a medium skillet over medium heat, add the turkey sausage (and 1 tbsp olive oil if the sausage is very lean). Cook, breaking it into small crumbles with a spatula, until browned and cooked through, 5–7 minutes. If there’s more than 1 tsp of rendered fat, drain off the excess. Remove sausage to a plate to cool slightly. 3. Sauté the vegetables: In the same skillet (no need to wash), add the diced onion and both bell peppers. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until softened and just starting to get some golden edges, 4–5 minutes. Add the chopped spinach and cook until wilted and most moisture has evaporated, 1–2 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool for 3–5 minutes so they don’t scramble the eggs on contact. 4. Make the egg base: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the 8 whole eggs and 1 cup liquid egg whites until well combined and slightly frothy. Add the milk, kosher salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, and crushed red pepper (if using). Whisk again until the seasonings are evenly distributed. Don’t shortcut this; uneven seasoning shows up in tiny portions. 5. Add cheese and herbs: Stir in the shredded sharp cheddar, grated Parmesan, and chopped parsley. Mix until the cheese is evenly coated in the egg mixture so it doesn’t clump in one or two cups. 6. Assemble in the muffin tin: Divide the cooked sausage evenly among the 12 muffin cups (about 1 heaping tablespoon per cup). Do the same with the sautéed vegetable mixture, gently spreading it so each cup has a roughly equal amount. Give the egg mixture a quick whisk, then pour it over the sausage and vegetables, filling each cup to about 3/4 full. If you have a little extra, top off the skimpiest cups—don’t overfill past the rim or they’ll mushroom and stick. 7. Bake: Place the muffin tin on the middle oven rack. Bake at 350°F for 18–22 minutes, until the egg cups are puffed, set around the edges, and the centers no longer look wet. A toothpick inserted in the center of one should come out mostly clean, with just a bit of moisture but no liquid egg. If your oven runs cool, they may take up to 24–26 minutes. 8. Cool and release: Remove the pan from the oven and let the egg cups cool in the tin for 5–7 minutes. Run a thin offset spatula or butter knife around the edges of each cup to loosen, then gently lift them out. If any resist, let them sit another couple minutes; the steam will help them release. 9. Store for the week: Let the egg cups cool to room temperature before storing. For the refrigerator, place them in an airtight container in a single layer (or separated with parchment) and refrigerate up to 4 days. For the freezer, wrap each cup individually in plastic wrap, then place in a zip-top freezer bag and freeze up to 2 months.
